title: Yellow Baby
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is a term newborn presenting with jaundice appearing after day 3-5 of life, clinically well-appearing, feeding well, gaining weight appropriately. Breastfeeding jaundice is the most common cause of prolonged neonatal unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia. Pathophysiology: inadequate breastfeeding intake → decreased stooling → increased enterohepatic circulation of bilirubin. Must distinguish from pathologic causes: hemolysis (ABO/Rh incompatibility, G6PD deficiency), sepsis, biliary atresia (conjugated), hypothyroidism. Key labs: total and direct bilirubin (unconjugated > conjugated by definition), CBC with reticulocyte count (anemia? hemolysis?), direct Coombs (immune hemolysis), G6PD screen. Plot on Bhutani nomogram for phototherapy threshold. Management: optimize breastfeeding (increase frequency, lactation consultation). Phototherapy if bilirubin exceeds threshold for gestational age and risk factors. Exchange transfusion if signs of bilirubin encephalopathy or failed phototherapy.
chief_complaint: Jaundice in otherwise well-appearing term newborn

stacks.label: CBC with differential + reticulocyte count
stacks.finding: Rule out hemolysis. Normal Hb = breastfeeding jaundice.

stacks.finding: Unconjugated > conjugated. Plot on Bhutani nomogram.

stacks.finding: Increase feeding frequency. Improve milk transfer.
